To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
for large doses, the total net pharmacologic effect of drugs is proportional to the drug dose and is independent of the pharmacokinetic system.
the asymptotics of AUCE is proportional (up to the order o (1)) to the time for which the drug stays above the threshold concentration and this time increases with the logarithm of the dose.

the total net direct effect AUCE for large doses is proportional to the integral of Cp(t) from the time t0 when the plasma concentration Cp(t) starts to decrease below EC50 to infinity and that this integral is asymptotically equal to the product of the dose and the integral of 1/Cp(t) from the same time t0 to infinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the asymptotics of AUCE for large doses and with the asymptotics for the time TC> EC50 for which the concentration of drug stays above EC50.
the asymptotic analysis of the total net effect of a drug as a function of the drug dose.
the asymptotic behavior of the total net effect of a drug as the drug dose tends to infinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymptotic behavior of the total net drug effect is determined by the asymptotic behavior for large doses of the drug plasma concentration and the drug concentration threshold level.
the AUCE of drugs with a linear pharmacokinetic system and a linear Emax model for the pharmacodynamic effect is proportional to the natural logarithm of drug plasma dose for large doses.
for the Emax model the asymptotics of AUCE is proportional with the logarithm of dose and that the asymptotics of its first derivative is proportional to 1/dose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a given drug dose the asymptotics of AUCE is determined by the asymptotics of TC>EC50 and the asymptotics of Cp for large dose.
the asymptotics of AUCE are proportional to the time for which drug concentration stays above EC50 and the latter time is proportional to the dose for large doses.
the total net pharmacologic effect is proportional to the dose for large doses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymptotics of AUCE as a function of drug dose is determined by the asymptotics of TC>EC50 as a function of the drug dose.
the AUCE of a drug with the Emax model is proportional to the drug dose for large drug doses.
the asymptotics of AUCE as a function of drug dose is determined by the asymptotics of TC>EC50 as a function of dose.
